function: Excluded, no_learning (p. 9): joint channel estimation and user localization done by an iterative variational Bayesian inference algorithm with closed-form updates and hand-set priors; no trained model.
notes: Identity: the PDF is arXiv:2403.01093v1; its title and six authors match the Crossref record of the DOI (IEEE TWC 23(9), 11309-11324), so it was graded. Reason no_learning: the 'variational Bayesian learning' is model-based approximate Bayesian inference run on the measurements of each realization, with no training data, training phase, or trained parameters. p. 9: "Our proposed algorithm is an iterative algorithm developed to approximate the true posterior distribution via mean-field factorization, KL divergence minimization, and alternating optimization." p. 1: "the joint channel and location estimation problem has a closed-form solution in each iteration". p. 10, Algorithm 1 only takes the priors and parameters and "collect measurements R", and the hyperparameters are fixed by hand: "ai = 10^5 and bi = 10^-3". Checks 1 and 2 pass (research article proposing a method). If the reviewer treated variational Bayes as learned, the later checks would not exclude it: joint channel estimation with localization would fit area 2 (localization alone is outside the seven areas); the AP and the user each have a single antenna but there is a 20x20 reflecting RIS (p. 3: "an access point (AP) equipped with a single antenna and single antenna user"; Table I, p. 10), so check 6 passes; simulation results are given in Figs. 2-10 (pp. 11-13). Baselines are a quasi-Newton/ML estimator [38], PSO [36], and the BCRB (p. 10).
